title: Serum–Ascites Albumin Gradient for Early POPF prediction
summary:
Background: After surgery on part of the pancreas, a leak can occur at the cut surface. Digestive juice from the pancreas then escapes into the abdomen. This can cause inflammation, delay healing and sometimes make further procedures necessary. After the operation, a thin tube (drain) is therefore placed in the abdomen to let fluid escape. So far, this fluid is tested for a digestive enzyme to detect such leaks. However, this test is not always reliable.

Research question: We want to find out whether a protein found in the blood (albumin) can better predict, early after surgery, whether a significant leak will occur. To do this, we compare the amount of this protein in the blood with the amount in the drain fluid. If the prediction is reliable, drains could be removed earlier in patients without problems. This would spare them discomfort and risks.

Methods: We observe adults who undergo pancreatic surgery. On the first, third and fifth day after surgery, the protein is measured in the blood and in the drain fluid. There is no additional treatment. Doctors decide on treatment and on drain removal as usual, independently of these measurements. Afterwards, we examine whether the measured values are related to the later occurrence of a significant leak, and we compare them with the test used so far.

interventions.name: Postoperative measurement of the serum-ascites albumin gradient (SAAG = serum albumin − drain fluid albumin) on postoperative days 1, 3 and 5 after partial pancreatectomy. This is a purely observational study without any study-specific intervention; postoperative management, including drain removal,

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Elective partial pancreatic resection (classical or pylorus-preserving pancreaticoduodenectomy, distal pancreatectomy, duodenum-preserving pancreatic head resection, enucleation or other limited resection)
Intraoperative placement of at least one surgical drain
Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Total pancreatectomy
Multivisceral resection
Intraoperative liver cirrhosis
Emergency surgery
Redo pancreatic surgery
Lack of ability for informed consent
No intraoperative drain placement
